# Pesher Psalms Column 2 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Pesher Psalms Column 2 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 2:1 — Psalm 37:14 — "draws out his sword" vs. "draw their swords"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "The wicked-one draws-out his sword" | Singular, literal Hebrew form |
| LOGOS | "The wicked draws his sword" | Singular, standard English |
| PNEUMA | "The wicked draw their swords" | Plural for English naturalness |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted singular (LOGOS). The Hebrew is singular (*rasha*), and the pesher applies it to specific groups.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:1-2 — "poor and needy" vs. "poor and helpless"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the poor-one and the needy-one" | Literal with hyphenated singulars |
| LOGOS | "the poor and needy" | Standard Psalmic pair |
| PNEUMA | "the poor and helpless" | "Helpless" for emotional impact |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the poor and the needy" (LOGOS pattern with EMET's article). Standard biblical word pair *ani ve-evyon*.

**Status:** Resolved — compromise of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:4 — "time of trial" vs. "time of testing" vs. "time of crisis"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "time of trial" | *et ha-masah* — literal |
| LOGOS | "time of testing" | Theological precision |
| PNEUMA | "time of crisis" | Modern impact |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET "time of trial" — captures both senses of testing and tribulation without modernizing.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 2:4 — "men of his council" vs. "those in his inner circle"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "men of his council" | Literal *anshei atsato* |
| LOGOS | "men of his council" | Standard scholarly rendering |
| PNEUMA | "those in his inner circle" | Modern accessibility |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "men of his council" (EMET/LOGOS). This is a technical organizational term in Qumran texts.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:6 — "ruthless ones" vs. "violent ones" vs. "brutal foreign nations"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "ruthless-ones of the nations" | Literal *aritsei ha-goyim* |
| LOGOS | "violent ones of the nations" | Slight interpretive shift |
| PNEUMA | "brutal foreign nations" | Dynamic condensation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "ruthless ones of the nations" — *aritsim* means "ruthless/tyrants," closer to EMET than LOGOS. PNEUMA loses the partitive construction.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 2:9 — "plotted to destroy" vs. "conspired to wipe out"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "plotted to destroy" | Standard literal |
| LOGOS | "plotted to destroy" | Same as EMET |
| PNEUMA | "conspired to wipe out" | More dramatic |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "plotted to destroy" (EMET/LOGOS). Accurate and restrained.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:12-13 — Psalm 37:16 rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Better is the little of the righteous-one" | Genitive construction preserved |
| LOGOS | "Better is the little that the righteous has" | Relative clause, more readable |
| PNEUMA | "The little that a good person has is worth more" | Completely restructured |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS — faithful to the Hebrew while natural in English. PNEUMA's restructuring loses the Psalmic register.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:16 — "chosen ones" vs. "elect" vs. "God's chosen ones"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "His chosen-ones" | Literal *bechirav* |
| LOGOS | "His elect" | Formal theological term |
| PNEUMA | "God's chosen ones" | Explicit divine reference |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "His chosen ones" — combines EMET's "chosen ones" with the possessive pronoun. "Elect" (LOGOS) is overly theological; PNEUMA's "God's" is an interpretive addition.

**Status:** Resolved — compromise.

---

**Total disagreements for Column 2: 8**
